liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station** (3 reviews): Terrapin and its following jam last roughly eighteen minutes and are called awesome; Attendee says the Terrapin, with Garcia playing amid incense smoke, is the most memorable moment of the night [16][18][19]
- **Jam** (1 other source): The post-Terrapin jam began with the full band, then continued without Garcia, then with Hornsby and the drummers [3]
- **That Would Be Something** (1 review): Reviewer says Dick's Picks 17 was chosen partly because of the first performance of That Would Be Something [25]
- **Help on the Way** (1 review): The Help>Slip>Franklin's sequence is praised as outstanding [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Help on the Way / Slipknot**: rare: 8 archived performances [26]
- **crowd chant & tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- Earliest performances in the archive: That Would Be Something [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-09-25.schoeps.andrewf.84858.sbeok.flac1648** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 170 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer prefers this Schoeps matrix to the Dick's Picks release because the crowd is heard clearly [22]
- **gd1991-09-25.aud.andrewf.84857.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 170 min [2]
- **gd1991-09-25.fob.bk4011.brennecke-young.gems.101442.flac**: source not stated; 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1991-09-25.177604.senn.me88.rogosa.goldey.flac2496**: source not stated; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd91-09-25.nak.dodd.16667.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 3.67/5 by 15 [13]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording decent, with the crowd's energy audible and the Dead's sound quality strong [14]

## Around the show

- Front-row-center attendee recalls incense burning behind Garcia, smoke swirling around his head while he jammed intensely with head down [18]
- Reviewer ranks this the weakest of the Boston Garden run, yet considers the portion after Space excellent [15]
- Reviewer calls it one of 1991's five best shows, saying a single night turned mediocre playing into something transcendent [16]
- Reviewer finds the show sloppy, with blown lyrics and onstage trouble, and doubts it merited a Dick's Pick, comparing debate to Cornell 77 [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-09-25.schoeps.andrewf.84858.sbeok.flac1648**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Schoeps CMC3/MK4 (ORTF) > unknown power supply > Panasonic SV-255 (lead deck) > Coax SPDIF > Casio DA-7 Dat (first deck out) > Agfa Dat tape. Mics on 7-foot… [1]. Also: 48kHz archival FLAC file-set from the Schoeps recording, not burnable to CDR; a 44.1kHz set is for CDs; A 0.702-second dropout in Tennessee Jed was mended; Soundforge made fades and TLH did FLAC and checksums [1]
- **gd1991-09-25.aud.andrewf.84857.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Schoeps CMC3/MK4 (ORTF) > unknown power supply > Panasonic SV-255 (lead deck) > Coax SPDIF > Casio DA-7 Dat (first deck out) > Agfa Dat tape. Mics on 7-foot… [2]. Also: A 0.702-second dropout in Tennessee Jed was mended with Soundforge; discs two and three can be rejoined seamlessly [2]
- **gd1991-09-25.fob.bk4011.brennecke-young.gems.101442.flac**: taped by James Young and Clay Brennecke; transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: Lineage: Master DAT Recording Equipment: B&K 4011 110º ORTF > Neumann BS 48i-2> Modified Sony TCD D-10 Pro Recording Location: FOB [3]
- **gd1991-09-25.177604.senn.me88.rogosa.goldey.flac2496**: taped by Dan Rogosa; transferred by Mark Goldey; source: 2x Sennheiser ME 88s (stand, OTS) > TCD-D3 > line out > TCD-D5 (Dolby B) [4]. Also: Taper Dan recorded this fifth of six Boston Garden shows on DAT and cassette; speed was checked against his DAT; Queen Jane, Drums and the Not Fade Away chant were patched in from Dan's DAT recording [4]
- **gd91-09-25.nak.dodd.16667.sbeok.shnf**: source: Nakamichi CM300 + CP4REAR > d-5>cm >cdrTaped and discs kindly provided by Mark HorvathEac > cool edit pro > shntool > cdwav > shnv3 By Ernie Dodd [13]. Also: Reviewer notes this show is released as Dick's Picks 17; Reviewer says no soundboard circulated for this show, though audience tapes from 1991 were good [19][25]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Boston Garden - September 25, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/september-25-1991) [27]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1991-09-25 Wed Boston Garden, Boston, MA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1305967886717/grateful-dead-1991-09-25-wed-boston) [31]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1991-09-25 Boston Garden, Boston, MA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1991-09-25-boston-garden-boston-ma-usa/) [32]
